text:
vikram: quick thought — could we add a "what-if" role simulator in the console so tenant admins can preview routing/quota effects before rolling out roles?

maria: +1. this would help avoid surprise throttles during canaries.

ashley: curious — do you mean simulate both routing policy (regional/cost tier) and quota enforcement? or just permission visibility?

vikram: both. e.g., show: which route a request would hit (hosted/dedicated/private), whether quota would block, and estimated cost delta. basically a dry-run of routing + quota eval for a given principal.

ben: sounds great but big API question: should simulation reuse the real authz evaluation service or be a separate sandboxed evaluator? reusing might leak production traffic patterns into sim logs.

megan: from UX perspective we need results fast (<2s ideally). sandboxed evaluator might need a cached view of route snapshots. can we do incremental: quick approximate sim using precomputed routing table, then a full sim with more detail async?

vikram: propose two modes: quick-preview (approx, local cache, instant) + deep-run (accurate, async, longer). quick-preview used in UI, deep-run available to export. deep-run can also produce a minimal audit artifact.

maria: telemetry: we should emit a distinct event for sims, something like `role_sim.run` with flags {mode, route_snapshot_id, principal_hash, sample_req_count}. important for SLOs and cost tracking.

ben: API sketch for deep-run:
```
POST /api/v1/simulate
body: { principal: "service:foo", scope: ["routes:read"], sample_requests: [...], mode: "deep" }
resp: { id: "sim-123", status: "queued", estimated_cost: 0.12 }
GET /api/v1/simulate/sim-123 -> full report
```

ashley: question: who can run sims? tenant admins only? or any role with `simulate:*`? we need RBAC gating otherwise folks will run expensive sims.

megan: agree gate it. UI only shows simulator to admins and delegated reviewers. Also surface a clear note: "simulation uses policy snapshots and may estimate cost; not a guarantee" :eyes:

vikram: ops concern: deep-run could be exploited to probe capacity. Add rate limits and quota on sim runs per org. Also block sims that request >N sample_requests or very broad scope.

ben: implementation note — reuse evaluation logic but run it against a read-only snapshot of routing table + quota state (snapshots stored as metadata). snapshots updated on every policy rollout. this avoids using live production state.

maria: nice. snapshotting also gives deterministic diffs for rollouts. we can show "before/after" by comparing current snapshot vs candidate snapshot (what-if a role change is applied).

megan: UI mock idea: left panel choose principal, middle panel specify change (add role X / remove scope Y), right panel shows routing map + quota heatmap + estimated token cost per percentile. small inline chart for latency distribution.

ashley: minimal MVP: only support per-principal "what-if add/remove role" and single-sample request template. no bulk. keep UI simple.

vikram: agree MVP scope. action items:
- ben: prototype API (POST/GET) + snapshot read-only mode (owner)
- megan: 2 quick mocks for quick-preview vs deep-run
- ashley: RBAC gating proposal and rate-limit thresholds
- maria: telemetry events + snapshot lifecycle rules

ben: I can start API proto tomorrow. will add `simulate.run` audit logs to the existing audit stream.

megan: I'll put mocks in Figma and tag ashley for review.

ashley: I'll draft RBAC rules and a console flag. propose default "off" for non-enterprise orgs.

devex-bot: Reminder: create an RFC doc and link to the SDK team if API shape changes affect client libs.

vikram: thanks all. +1 to RFC. We'll iterate next week in sync. :thumbsup:
